questions.question: Which of the following is used to identify every computer in the internet?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**IP address**__".

• **Every machine** on the Internet has a **unique** **identifying** number, called an** IP Address.**
 
• The IP stands for Internet Protocol, which is the language that computers use to **communicate** **over** the **Internet**.
 
• A protocol is a pre-defined way that someone who wants to use a **service** **talks** with that service.
 
• The "someone" could be a person, but more often it is a computer program like a Web browser.
 
• A typical IP address looks like this: 216.27.61.137.
 
• To make it easier for us humans to remember, IP addresses are normally expressed in decimal format as a dotted-decimal number like the one above.
 
• But computers communicate in binary form.

questions.question: It connects all types of computers across the world. Which communication technology is being spoken about here?

questions.question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to copy the selected data in MS-Word 365?

• **Ctrl + C **is a universal keyboard shortcut on Microsoft systems that copies the selected text or item to the clipboard.
 
• **This shortcut is used across many applications, not just MS Word.**

• The copied data can then be pasted elsewhere using the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + V.**
 
• This is a quicker and more efficient way of copying data than using the mouse to select** 'Copy' from the right-click context menu or from the 'Edit' menu in the toolbar.**
 
• It's also worth noting that the original data remains in place after the copy operation, allowing it to be copied to multiple locations if desired.

questions.question: What is an output device that transforms the signal from the computer's sound card into audio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A speaker is an output device that transforms digital signals processed by the computer's sound card into **audible sound waves **or **audio**.
 
• The sound card sends an electrical signal to the speaker, and then the speaker converts this electrical signal into physical vibrations (**sound waves**) that we can hear.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Device
 Input/Output Device
 Function / Signal Conversion
 
 
 
 

 Plotter
 Output
 Plotters convert digital vector images sent from the computer into physical plots on various materials, usually paper or plastic, using pens or other drawing instruments. The computer sends data to the plotter specifying the colors and shapes in the image, and the plotter then creates the image on the output medium.
 
 

 Graphics Card
 Output
 The graphics card takes digital visual data from the processor and converts it into a signal that the monitor can display. The resulting output is what you see on your monitor. The graphics card is vital for rendering high-quality images quickly, especially for video games and high-definition videos.
 
 

 Monitor
 Output
 The monitor receives digital or analog signals from the graphics card and converts them into visible light displays. In a nutshell, the graphics card translates the data into signals the monitor can use, and the monitor displays these signals as the images you see on the screen.

questions.question: The symbol which is used to separate the user name and email server parts of an email is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**@**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "@" symbol is used to separate the user name from the email server in an email address.
 
• It is a standard convention in email addresses, ensuring correct routing of the message to the intended recipient.
 
• The "@" symbol was first chosen by Ray Tomlinson in 1971 as a way to distinguish between the user's name and their machine (server) name.
 
• This symbol is universally recognized and used in all email systems across the globe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Email Address Structure:**

 
 
• An email address typically has the format: username@domain.com
 
• **Username:** Identifies the email account holder.
 
• **Domain:** Specifies the mail server responsible for receiving and delivering the email. The domain usually follows the format: domain.extension (e.g., gmail.com, yahoo.com).
 
 
 
• **Importance of the "@" Symbol:**
 
 
• The "@" symbol separates the user's name from the domain name, making it possible to route the email to the correct server and user.
 
• It ensures the uniqueness of each email address, avoiding conflicts in email delivery.
 
 
 
• **History and Origin:**
 
 
• The "@" symbol has been used since the 16th century in commerce and accounting as a shorthand for "at the rate of."
 
• Ray Tomlinson, a computer engineer, selected the "@" symbol to denote the separation of the user and their host computer in email addresses in 1971.
 
 
 
• **Other Symbols in Email Addresses:**
 
 
• While the "@" symbol is mandatory, other symbols like periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_) can be used in the username portion.
 
• However, these symbols cannot be used consecutively or start/end the username.

questions.question: What is the full form of HTTP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hypertext Transfer Protocol__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol. Hypertext Transfer Protocol is an application protocol used for data communication. It is the base of data communication in the World Wide Web. It provides a standard for web browsers that facilitates users to exchange information over the internet.
 
• HTTP is used by most websites to access any file or page. HTTP is a request-response protocol in the client-server computing model. It is an application layer protocol designed within the framework of the Internet Protocol Suite.
 
• Hypertext - A text containing a link within it, is known as hypertext. If you click on a word on a webpage and it redirects you to a new page, it means you have clicked on a hypertext.​
 
• It is the protocol where encrypted HTTP data is transferred over a secure connection. It ensures data security over the network - mainly public networks like Wi-Fi.
 
• By virtue, HTTPS encryption is done bi-directionally, which means that the data is encrypted at both the client and server sides. Only the client can decode the information that comes from the server. So, HTTPS does the encryption of data between a client and a server, which protects against eavesdropping, forging of information, and tampering of data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• HTTPS is HTTP with encryption.
 
• The only difference between the two protocols is that HTTPS uses TLS (SSL) to encrypt normal HTTP requests and responses. As a result, HTTPS is far more secure than HTTP.
 
• A website that uses HTTP has http:// in its URL, while a website that uses HTTPS has https://.

questions.question: Which of the following fields tells the recipient what the message is about?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subject**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Subject** field in an email message is a brief description of the content of the message.
 
• It helps the recipient to understand the purpose or main idea of the message before opening it.
 
• A clear and concise subject line can increase the chances of the email being read and acted upon.
 
• It is a standard field in email messages, often displayed prominently in the recipient's inbox.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Date**

 
 
• This field indicates the date and time when the email was sent.
 
• It helps the recipient know when the email was composed and dispatched.
 
 
 
• **To**
 
 
• This field contains the email address of the main recipient(s) of the message.
 
• It is a mandatory field in an email, without which the email cannot be sent.
 
 
 
• **Signature**
 
 
• This is a block of text automatically appended at the end of an email message.
 
• It often contains the sender's name, contact information, and other relevant details.
 
• Signatures help in providing consistent contact information and can also be used for branding purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols is used to transfer files from one host to another over the internet?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**FTP**__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

FTP :

__
 
• **FTP** is a widely used network protocol for transferring files between computers over a **TCP/IP-based network,** such as the **Internet**.
 
• FTP lets people and applications exchange and shares data within their offices and across the **Internet**.
 
• FTP was one of the first technologies developed to solve this common need, and it remains, with several generations of enhancements, the second most popular protocol used today (after HTTP or the "**World Wide Web**").

**Applications :**

 
• **Organizations** use FTP to **allow employees **to share files across different locations and branch offices.
 
• Employees use FTP to securely share files with coworkers and external business partners.
 
• **IT teams** use **FTP** to transfer data back to **DR (disaster recovery) sites.**
 
• Webmaster teams use FTP to transfer Web pages, Web application files, and images to their **Web server.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**IP :**

 
• A**n IP address** is a **unique** **identifier** assigned to a device or domain that connects to the **Internet**
 
• Each IP address is a series of characters, such as '192.168.1.1'. Via DNS resolvers, which translate human-readable domain names into IP addresses, users are able to access websites without memorizing this complex series of characters. 
 
• Each IP packet will contain both the IP address of the device or domain sending the packet and the IP address of the intended recipient, much like how both the destination address and the return address are included on a piece of mail.
 
• **IP** Address is either a f**our-byte (IPv4) **or an** sixteen-byte (IPv6) **address.
 
• A device attached with IP Address can retrieve by **RARP** protocol.
 
• IP Address operates in the **network layer.**
 
• IP Address identifies the connection of the device on the network.
 
• IP Address modifies with the time and environment.
 
• IP Addresses can be found by a** third party.**

 

**UDP :**

 
• **User Datagram Protocol (UDP)** is a **Transport Layer protocol.**
 
• UDP is a part of the Internet Protocol suite, referred to as **UDP/IP suite.** Unlike TCP**,** it is an unreliable and **connectionless** **protocol**.
 
• So, there is no need to establish a connection prior to data transfer. 
 
• Though Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is the dominant transport layer protocol used with most Internet services; provides assured delivery, reliability, and much more but all these services cost us additional overhead and latency.
 
• Here, UDP comes into the picture. For real-time services like computer gaming, voice or video communication, live conferences; we need UDP.
 
• Since high performance is needed, UDP permits packets to be dropped instead of **processing** **delayed** **packets**.
 
• There is no error checking in UDP, so it also saves bandwidth. 
 
• User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is more efficient in terms of both latency and bandwidth. 
 
• **UDP** **header** is an **8-bytes fixed** and simple **header**, while for TCP it may vary from** 20 bytes to 60 bytes.**
 
• The **first 8 Bytes** contains all necessary header information and the remaining part consist of data.
 
• **UDP** **port** **number** fields are each 16 bits long, therefore the range for port numbers defined from **0 to 65535; port number 0 i**s reserved.
 
• Port numbers help to distinguish different user requests or processes. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbff717ff7a30cf48cc3b3fe42576bf35431a6c943487091aa4a0733bb0d3f11.png] 

**TCP :**

 
• **TCP stands** for **Transmission Control Protocol.**
 
• It is a **transport** **layer** **protocol** that facilitates the transmission of packets from **source** to **destination**.
 
• It is a connection-oriented protocol that means it establishes the connection prior to the communication that occurs between the computing devices in a network.
 
• This protocol is used with an IP protocol, so together, they are referred to as a** TCP/IP.**
 
• The main functionality of the TCP is to take the data from the **application layer.**
 
• Then it divides the data into several packets, provides numbering to these packets, and **finally** **transmits** these packets to the **destination**.
 
• The TCP, on the other side, will **reassemble** the **packets** and **transmits** them to the** application layer.**
 
• As we know that TCP is a connection-oriented protocol, so the connection will remain established until the communication is not completed between the sender and the receiver.

• Ctrl+Shift+P: Changes the font size to the next larger preset size for the selected text. It is useful for quickly adjusting the font size.

• Ctrl+L: Left-aligns the selected text. It aligns the text horizontally to the left margin.
 
• Ctrl+R: Right-aligns the selected text. It aligns the text horizontally to the right margin.
 
• Ctrl+J: Justifies the selected text. It aligns the text both horizontally to the left and right margins, creating even spacing between words.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of network?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROR**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ROR** does not refer to any type of network.
 
• In the context of networks, common types include **LAN, MAN, and WAN**.
 
• A network typically refers to a group of computers and other devices connected together to share resources.
 
• **LAN (Local Area Network)**, **MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)**, and **WAN (Wide Area Network)** are well-known network types based on their geographical spread.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **LAN**__

 __
 
• LAN (Local Area Network) typically covers a small geographic area like a home, office, or building.
 
• LANs are known for their high data transfer rates and limited geographic range.
 
• Examples include a network within a school or a small office network.
 
 
 
• **MAN**__
 __
 
• **MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)** spans a larger area than a LAN, such as a city or a large campus.
 
• It is designed to extend over several kilometers and often used to connect multiple LANs within a city.
 
• MANs are often used by organizations with multiple buildings within a city.
 
 
 
• **WAN**__
 
 
• **WAN (Wide Area Network)** covers a broad area, potentially spanning countries or even continents.
 
• WANs are used to connect multiple LANs over large distances, using various communication channels like leased lines, satellites, or the internet.
 
• The Internet is the most well-known example of a WAN.

questions.question: What is the full form of TCP/IP, with reference to internet protocols?

options.text: Transfer Control Protocol and Internet Protocol
Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol
Transmission Control Protocol and International Protocol

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **TCP/IP** stands for **Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol.**
 
• The Internet protocol suite is the **conceptual model** and **set of communications protocols** used in the **Internet and similar computer networks.**
 
• It is commonly known as **TCP/IP **because the **foundational protocols** in the suite are the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and the Internet Protocol (IP). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) **is an application-layer protocol for transmitting hypermedia documents, such as HTML.
 
• **SMTP **stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. 
 
• **The File Transfer Protocol (FTP)** is a standard communication protocol used for the transfer of computer files from a server to a client on a computer network.
